correctness.rationale: The diagonal moment reduction is algebraically exact; positive weights permit logs and eliminate hidden domains. The lower bound on every increment and the upper weighted sum imply the optimal constant. Equality conditions are necessary and sufficient because all coefficients are positive. A globally admissible finite pulse realizes the upper bound, an isolated negative step realizes the lower, and the slow ramp has arbitrarily small errors but exact scalar-shift distance 1/4. The actual standalone checker reports 576 rational pulses, 15000 generic cases, 27 lower witnesses, 12 ramps. The analytical proof, not finite testing, handles all n and j.

value.rationale: Two exact one-sided Embry moments characterize quasinormality; near equality raises a natural functional-analytic stability problem. The finding gives a sharp scale-invariant local perturbation bound for every positive unilateral shift and every higher moment order, characterizes saturation, and proves a sharp qualitative boundary preventing uniform global operator-norm stability. Exact pulses prove optimality and the slow-ramp example explains the essential distinction between local and global stability.
